question: when to sow wheat in Punjab
answer: In Punjab, sow wheat from October 25 to November 25. Early sowing (Oct 25-Nov 10) in central Punjab, mid-November in southern Punjab. Delay reduces yield by 1-1.5% per day. Optimum temperature: 20-25°C.

question: wheat sowing time in Sindh
answer: In Sindh, sow wheat from November 1-30. Lower Sindh: Nov 1-20, Upper Sindh: Nov 10-30. Use short-duration varieties if sowing after December. Sukkur region: best sowing Nov 15-25.

question: wheat sowing time in KPK
answer: In KPK, sow wheat from October 20 to November 15. Peshawar valley: Oct 25-Nov 15. D.I. Khan: Nov 1-20. Higher elevations: Oct 15-30. Use cold-tolerant varieties for late sowing.

question: wheat sowing time in Balochistan
answer: In Balochistan, sow wheat from October 15 to November 20. Quetta region: Oct 15-30, Sibi/Naseerabad: Nov 1-20. Use drought-tolerant varieties for rainfed areas.

question: can we sow wheat in december
answer: December sowing is not recommended as yield reduces 30-50%. If necessary, use short-duration varieties (130-140 days) like Punjab-2011, Sehar-2006. Increase seed rate by 20-25%. Expect 20-25 maunds/acre instead of 40+.

question: wheat sowing for rainfed areas
answer: For rainfed (Barani) areas: Sow Oct 15-30 to utilize residual moisture. Use drought-tolerant varieties: Chakwal-50, Dharabi-2011, Fatehjang-16. Seed rate: 50-60 kg/acre. Deep ploughing for moisture conservation.

question: best month for wheat sowing
answer: November is the best month for wheat sowing across Pakistan. Mid-November gives highest yields. October-end to November-25 is optimal window. Earlier sowing risks rust, later sowing reduces tillering.

question: wheat sowing after rice
answer: For rice-wheat system: Sow wheat immediately after rice harvest (Nov 10-30). Zero-till drill saves 10-15 days. Happy Seeder technology allows sowing in standing stubble. Use 25-30% higher seed rate.

question: wheat sowing after cotton
answer: Cotton-wheat system: Sow by Nov 30 maximum. Late cotton picking delays wheat. Use relay cropping: sow wheat 15 days before cotton harvest. Short-duration cotton varieties help timely wheat sowing.

question: wheat sowing after sugarcane
answer: Sugarcane-wheat system: Autumn-planted sugarcane (Sept-Oct) leaves no window for wheat. Instead, opt for wheat-sugarcane intercropping or ratoon management. Wheat sown in Feb as spring crop gives low yield.

question: seed rate for wheat per acre
answer: Recommended seed rate: 50-60 kg/acre (1-1.25 maunds). For late sowing: increase to 65-75 kg. For rainfed: 55-65 kg. For bold seeded varieties: 60-70 kg. Use certified seed for best germination.

question: wheat seed rate for drill sowing
answer: Drill sowing: 50-55 kg/acre. Maintain row spacing of 22.5-30 cm. For bed planting: 45-50 kg/acre on 60-70 cm beds (2 rows per bed). Adjust according to 1000-grain weight.

question: wheat seed rate for broadcasting
answer: Broadcasting: 65-75 kg/acre. Higher seed rate compensates for uneven germination. Cover seed by light ploughing or planking. Not recommended for optimal yield. Prefer drill or bed planting.

question: wheat seed treatment before sowing
answer: Treat wheat seed with fungicide: Carbendazim 2g or Tebuconazole 1.5g per kg seed. For termites: Chlorpyrifos 2-3ml/kg. Mix with water 20ml/kg, dry in shade 1-2 hours before sowing.

question: how to treat wheat seed for karnal bunt
answer: For Karnal bunt control: Treat seed with Vitavax (Carboxin) 2g/kg or Tilt (Propiconazole) 0.5ml/kg. Hot water treatment: 52°C for 10 minutes. Use resistant varieties like Inqalab-91, Uqab-2000.

question: wheat seed treatment for rust
answer: For rust control: Tebuconazole 1.5g/kg or Triadimefon 1g/kg seed treatment. Use resistant varieties: Aas-2011, Millat-2020. No seed treatment fully prevents rust - foliar sprays needed if rust appears.

question: wheat seed rate per acre in kg
answer: 50-60 kg per acre for timely sowing. 1 kg = approximately 25,000-30,000 grains. Target plant population: 100-120 plants per square meter. Adjust based on germination percentage.

question: wheat seed rate for hybrid varieties
answer: Hybrid wheat: 45-50 kg/acre due to higher tillering capacity. Not commonly grown in Pakistan. Available hybrids imported from China/India. 15-20% lower seed rate than conventional varieties.

question: best wheat varieties for Punjab
answer: Top varieties for Punjab: Galaxy-2013 (irrigated, high yield), Faisalabad-2008 (rust tolerant), Sehar-2006 (heat tolerant), Millat-2020 (new high yielder), Anaj-2017 (good chapati quality), Zincol-2016 (zinc enriched), Akbar-2019 (drought tolerant).

question: wheat varieties for Sindh
answer: Recommended for Sindh: Benazir-2013 (heat tolerant), Kiran-95 (salt tolerant), TD-1 (Tandojam developed), Marvi-2000 (irrigated), Khirman (late sowing), Sindhu-2016 (high yield), Imdad-2005 (rust resistant).

question: wheat varieties for rainfed areas
answer: Rainfed varieties: Chakwal-50 (drought tolerant), Dharabi-2011 (high yield under stress), Fatehjang-16 (short duration), NARC-2009 (rainfed), Barani-83 (old but reliable), Wafaq-2001 (medium maturity).

question: rust resistant wheat varieties
answer: Rust resistant: Aas-2011 (yellow rust resistant), Punjab-2011 (leaf rust resistant), Millat-2020 (triple rust resistant), Faisalabad-2008 (moderate resistance), Zincol-2016 (yellow rust resistant), Galaxy-2013 (adult plant resistance).

question: high yielding wheat varieties
answer: Highest yielders: Galaxy-2013 (55-65 maunds/acre), Millat-2020 (60+ maunds), Faisalabad-2008 (50-60 maunds), Anaj-2017 (50-55 maunds), Ujala-2016 (50-60 maunds), Pakistan-2013 (50-55 maunds).

question: biofortified wheat varieties
answer: Zinc-enriched: Zincol-2016, Akbar-2019. Iron-enriched: NR-421, NR-431. Developed by HarvestPlus and AARI. Contain 25-30% higher zinc than conventional varieties. Released 2016-2019.

question: heat tolerant wheat varieties
answer: Heat tolerant: Sehar-2006 (late sown), Benazir-2013 (Sindh), NARC-2011 (terminal heat), Mairaj-2008 (temperature up to 35°C), Punjab-2011 (moderate tolerance), Galaxy-2013 (good for central Punjab).

question: wheat varieties for early sowing
answer: Early sowing (Oct): Use varieties with longer duration: Inqalab-91 (140 days), Faisalabad-2008 (145 days), Punjab-2011 (150 days). Avoid early flowering in November-December. Moderate seeding rate.

question: wheat varieties for late sowing
answer: Late sowing (Dec): Use short duration varieties: Sehar-2006 (130 days), Punjab-2011 (135 days), AARI-2011 (130 days), Ujala-2016 (135 days). Increase seed rate by 25%. Compensate for less tillering.

question: wheat varieties for salt affected soils
answer: Salt tolerant: LU-26 (high tolerance), Kiran-95 (Sindh), Pasban-90, SARC-1, SARC-5, NR-7. For ECe 6-10 dS/m. Gypsum application recommended. Better germination in saline conditions.

question: land preparation for wheat
answer: After rice: 1 ploughing with disc harrow + 2 cultivations + planking. After cotton: 2 cultivations + planking. After fallow: 3 cultivations + 2 plankings. Deep ploughing every 3 years. Field leveling saves 20-30% irrigation water.

question: how to prepare field for wheat after rice
answer: Rice-wheat system challenges: 1. Zero-till drill sowing saves time/cost 2. Happy Seeder in standing stubble 3. If conventional: 1-2 disc harrowings, then rotavator/cultivator 4. Avoid puddling soil 5. Ensure fine tilth for seed-soil contact.

question: wheat bed planting method
answer: Bed planting: Make 60-70 cm beds with 2 rows per bed. Row spacing 20-25 cm, plant spacing 5-7 cm. Saves 30-40% irrigation water. Reduces lodging. Better root growth. Use bed planter attachment with tractor.

question: zero tillage wheat sowing
answer: Zero-till: Direct drilling with zero-till drill. Saves Rs. 3,000-4,000/acre in land prep. Sows 15 days earlier. Less weed pressure. Diesel saving 15-20 liters/acre. Available at Punjab Agriculture Department.

question: happy seeder technology for wheat
answer: Happy Seeder: Sows wheat in rice stubble without burning. Cuts and lifts stubble, sows seed, places stubble as mulch. Rs. 2,000-2,500/acre service charges. Subsidy available. Stops air pollution from stubble burning.

question: npk ratio for wheat
answer: Recommended NPK: 120-60-40 kg/hectare (48-24-16 kg/acre). For high yield target (50+ maunds): 150-75-50 kg/hectare. Adjust based on soil test. Phosphorus and potassium: full at sowing. Nitrogen: 3 splits.

question: urea for wheat per acre
answer: Urea requirement: 2-3 bags per acre (100-150 kg). Apply in 3 splits: 1 bag at sowing, 1 bag at first irrigation (20-25 days), 1 bag at second irrigation (45-50 days). For late sown: 2 splits only.

question: dap for wheat per acre
answer: DAP requirement: 1-1.5 bags per acre (50-75 kg). Apply full at sowing. Provides 18-27 kg phosphorus and 9-13.5 kg nitrogen. In P-deficient soils: 2 bags/acre. Combine with SOP/MOP for potassium.

question: potash for wheat per acre
answer: Potash (MOP/SOP): 0.5-1 bag per acre (25-50 kg). Apply full at sowing. Essential for grain filling, drought tolerance, disease resistance. K-deficient soils: sandy soils, intensive cropping, 1 bag/acre minimum.

question: zinc for wheat
answer: Zinc sulphate: 10-15 kg/hectare (4-6 kg/acre) at sowing. Mix with fertilizer or apply as foliar spray 0.5% at 20-30 days. Zinc deficiency: white/yellow bands on leaves, stunted growth. Corrects with 2-3 year residual effect.

question: boron for wheat
answer: Boron: 1-2 kg/hectare in B-deficient soils (sandy, alkaline). Apply at sowing or foliar spray 0.2% at booting stage. Deficiency: hollow grains, poor pollination. Use borax (11% B) or solubor (20% B).

question: sulfur for wheat
answer: Sulfur: 15-20 kg/hectare. Sources: SSP (12% S), Ammonium sulfate (24% S), Gypsum (18% S). Deficiency: pale leaves, reduced protein. Beneficial for chapati quality. Apply at sowing.

question: fym for wheat
answer: Farm Yard Manure: 10-15 tons/hectare (4-6 tons/acre) 15-20 days before sowing. Well-rotted FYM. Improves soil structure, water holding capacity, microbial activity. Reduces fertilizer requirement by 25% in long term.

question: biofertilizer for wheat
answer: Biozote/N-Fix: Azospirillum/bacteria culture. Mix 1 packet (500g) with 15-20 kg seed using jaggery water. Fixes 20-30 kg N/hectare. Phosphorus Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB): releases fixed P. Apply with 25% less chemical fertilizer.

question: fertilizer schedule for wheat
answer: At sowing: Full P, K, Zn + 1/3 N. 20-25 days (1st irrigation): 1/3 N. 45-50 days (2nd irrigation): 1/3 N. 70-75 days (3rd irrigation): Top up N if crop looks yellow. Stop N after flowering.

question: irrigation schedule for wheat
answer: 4-5 irrigations: 1st: Crown root initiation (20-25 days) - CRITICAL, 2nd: Tillering (45-50 days), 3rd: Flowering (75-80 days) - CRITICAL, 4th: Grain filling (100-105 days), 5th: Dough stage (120-125 days, optional).

question: critical stages of irrigation in wheat
answer: Most critical: Crown root initiation (1st irrigation) - determines tillers. Flowering stage (3rd irrigation) - pollination. Grain filling (4th irrigation) - grain weight. Water stress at these stages reduces yield 30-50%.

question: first irrigation in wheat
answer: First irrigation at 20-25 days after sowing (crown root initiation). Delay increases tiller mortality. Early (before 20 days) causes waterlogging. Light irrigation of 2.5-3 acre-inches. For sandy soil: 15-18 days.

question: last irrigation in wheat
answer: Last irrigation at grain filling (100-105 days) or dough stage (120-125 days). Stop 10-15 days before harvest. Late irrigation delays maturity, increases lodging risk. For timely harvest, drain field 7 days before harvest.

question: wheat irrigation for sandy soil
answer: Sandy soil: 6-8 light irrigations at 10-12 day intervals. First at 15-18 days. Higher frequency, lower volume. Mulching with crop residue reduces evaporation. Add FYM/green manure to improve water holding capacity.

question: wheat irrigation for clay soil
answer: Clay soil: 4-5 irrigations at 18-25 day intervals. Avoid over-irrigation. Drain excess water. Bed planting improves drainage. First irrigation at 25-28 days. Later irrigations at longer intervals.

question: drip irrigation for wheat
answer: Drip irrigation: Saves 40-50% water. Increases yield 15-20%. Feasible in water-scarce areas. Initial cost: Rs. 120,000-150,000/acre. Government subsidy 60-80%. Drip tape or inline drip. Particularly for bed planting.

question: sprinkler irrigation for wheat
answer: Sprinkler irrigation: Suitable for sandy/undulating fields. Water saving 30-40%. Uniform distribution. Initial cost: Rs. 80,000-100,000/acre. 60% subsidy. Operating cost Rs. 1,000-1,500/acre/irrigation.

question: herbicides for wheat
answer: Broadleaf weeds: Buctril M (Bromoxynil+MCPA) 400ml/acre, Starane M (Fluroxypyr) 300ml/acre. Grassy weeds: Puma Super (Fenoxaprop) 500ml/acre, Axial (Pinoxaden) 300ml/acre. Apply 30-40 days after sowing.

question: wild oat control in wheat
answer: Wild oat (Jangli Jai): Puma Super 500ml/acre at 3-4 leaf stage (30-35 days). Axial 300ml/acre. Atlantis 14.4g (Mesosulfuron+Iodosulfuron) 200g/acre. Apply when weeds are actively growing. Use flat fan nozzle.

question: canada thistle control in wheat
answer: Canada thistle (Lehli): Buctril M 400ml/acre at 3-5 leaf stage. Starane M 300ml/acre. Apply 30-40 days after sowing. Repeat in subsequent years. Competitive varieties with good tillering suppress thistle.

question: broadleaf weed control in wheat
answer: Broadleaf weeds (Maina, Bathu, Peeli Buti): Buctril M 400ml/acre, Starane M 300ml/acre, Logran 200g/acre, 2,4-D Na Salt 600g/acre. Avoid 2,4-D before tillering (causes twisting).

question: when to spray herbicide in wheat
answer: Spray at 30-40 days after sowing (3-4 leaf stage of weeds). Morning hours, no wind, no rain forecast. Temperature 15-25°C. Avoid moisture stress. Use 100-120 liters water/acre. Flat fan nozzle 80-110 degrees.

question: aphid control in wheat
answer: Aphid: Imidacloprid 250ml/acre, Confidor 250ml/acre, Actara 80g/acre, Dimethoate 500ml/acre. Spray when 10+ aphids per tiller. Ladybird beetles natural predator. Avoid pyrethroids - kill beneficial insects.

question: armyworm control in wheat
answer: Armyworm (Gandar): Chlorpyrifos 800ml/acre, Lorsban 800ml/acre, Coragen 60ml/acre, Belt 40ml/acre. Spray in evening. Check field borders first. Fill trenches around field. Natural enemies: parasitic wasps.

question: termite control in wheat
answer: Termite: Chlorpyrifos 5L/acre soil treatment before sowing. Seed treatment with Confidor 5ml/kg. Drenching at termite appearance. Remove previous crop residues. Deep summer ploughing exposes termites.

question: yellow rust control in wheat
answer: Yellow rust: Folicur (Tebuconazole) 250ml/acre, Tilt (Propiconazole) 250ml/acre, Nativo (Trifloxystrobin+Tebuconazole) 200g/acre, Amistar Top (Azoxystrobin+Difenoconazole) 200ml/acre. Spray at rust appearance. Resistant varieties: Aas-2011, Millat-2020.

question: karnal bunt control in wheat
answer: Karnal bunt: Seed treatment with Vitavax 2g/kg or Tilt 0.5ml/kg. Avoid irrigation at flowering. Resistant varieties: Inqalab-91, Uqab-2000. Quarantine: disease-free seed. No effective foliar spray.

question: powdery mildew control in wheat
answer: Powdery mildew: Sulfur dust 5kg/acre, Karathane 400ml/acre, Tilt 250ml/acre. Avoid dense canopy, excess N. Resistant varieties. Appears in cool humid weather. Improve air circulation.

question: leaf rust control in wheat
answer: Leaf rust: Mancozeb 500g/acre, Tilt 250ml/acre, Folicur 250ml/acre. Spray at pustule appearance. Resistant varieties: Punjab-2011, Faisalabad-2008. Apply early before epidemic.

question: wheat harvesting time
answer: Harvest March-May, 110-130 days after sowing. Northern Punjab: April 15-May 15. Southern Punjab: March 25-April 20. Sindh: March 1-30. KPK: May 1-June 15. Balochistan: May-June.

question: how to know wheat is ready for harvest
answer: Signs: Grains hard (biting test), straw golden yellow, moisture 20-25%, flag leaf dried, grains not dented by fingernail. Harvest at physiological maturity. Late harvest: lodging, shattering, rain damage.

question: wheat yield per acre in Pakistan
answer: National average: 30-35 maunds/acre. Punjab: 32-38, Sindh: 28-32, KPK: 25-30, Balochistan: 20-25. Progressive farmers: 50-55 maunds. Research stations: 65+ maunds. Yield gap 40% due to practices.

question: how to increase wheat yield
answer: 1. Timely sowing (Nov 1-20) 2. Certified seed 3. Balanced NPK + Zn 4. Weed-free field 5. 4-5 irrigations at critical stages 6. Disease/pest control 7. Zero-till/Happy Seeder 8. Bed planting. Add 15-20 maunds/acre.

question: how to store wheat at home
answer: Dry to 12-14% moisture. Clean, remove broken grains. Store in metal bins/gunny bags. Neem leaves/bavistin tablets for insect control. Avoid moisture. Check periodically. For long term: fumigation with aluminum phosphide tablets (2-3 per ton).

question: wheat storage pests
answer: Major storage pests: Khapra beetle (Trogoderma), Red flour beetle (Tribolium), Rice weevil (Sitophilus), Lesser grain borer. Control: Cleaning, drying, proper storage, fumigation, neem leaves, camphor. Government godowns: scientific storage.

question: wheat cultivation cost per acre
answer: Total cost: Rs. 45,000-55,000/acre. Breakdown: Land prep: 5,000-6,000, Seed: 4,000-5,000, Fertilizer: 12,000-15,000, Irrigation: 6,000-8,000, Pesticides: 3,000-5,000, Harvesting: 5,000-7,000, Land rent: 10,000-12,000.

question: wheat profit per acre
answer: Income: Yield 35 maunds × Rs. 1,500-1,800/maund = Rs. 52,500-63,000. Cost: Rs. 45,000-55,000. Net profit: Rs. 10,000-20,000/acre. Progressive farmers (50 maunds): Rs. 75,000-90,000 income, Rs. 30,000-40,000 profit.

question: wheat support price 2024
answer: Government announced wheat support price: Rs. 1,500-1,800 per 40kg. Punjab: Rs. 1,650, Sindh: Rs. 1,600, KPK: Rs. 1,550, Balochistan: Rs. 1,500. Procurement centers operate March-June. Premium for quality grain.

question: rice nursery sowing time
answer: Sow nursery May 20-June 20. Basmati: May 25-June 15. Irri: May 15-June 10. Coarse varieties: May 10-June 5. Nursery age: 25-30 days for transplanting. Use 8-10 kg seed/acre nursery (covers 1 acre).

question: rice transplanting time
answer: Transplant June 15-July 15. Basmati: June 20-July 15 optimum. Irri: June 10-30. Late transplanting (after July 20) reduces yield 20-30%. Early transplanting (before June 10) has more pest/disease pressure.

question: rice nursery preparation
answer: Nursery area: 1/10 acre for 1 acre. Raised beds 1.5m wide, any length. Apply FYM 5 kg/sq.m + DAP 50g/sq.m. Sow sprouted seed @ 80g/sq.m. Maintain thin water layer. Remove weeds. 25-30 days seedling age.

question: dapog method rice nursery
answer: Dapog method: Seed on banana leaves/plastic sheets. 1kg seed/ sq.m. Sprout for 24-48 hours. Spread 2cm thick. Cover with leaves. Water twice daily. 9-11 days seedlings ready. Saves time, space, water.

question: best basmati rice varieties
answer: Super Basmati: extra-long grain, strong aroma, 130-140 days, yield 25-30 maunds/acre. Basmati-515: high yield 30-35 maunds, good aroma. Basmati-198: early (120 days), yield 28-32 maunds. PK-1121: extra-long grain, export quality.

question: irri rice varieties in Pakistan
answer: IRRI-6: coarse, 100-110 days, yield 50-60 maunds. KS-282: medium grain, 115-120 days, yield 55-65 maunds. NIAB-6: fine grain, 110-115 days, yield 45-50 maunds. DR-82: short duration, yield 40-45 maunds.

question: hybrid rice in Pakistan
answer: Hybrid rice: RH-257, PHB-71, Arize H-6444, Savana-444. Yield 60-80 maunds/acre. 120-130 days. Better seedling vigor. Higher seed cost Rs. 1,000-1,500/kg. Requires 3-4 kg/acre. Bt rice not commercially available.

question: rice varieties for Sindh
answer: Sindh varieties: IRRI-6 (90% area), DR-82, DR-83, Sarshar, Latif, Shua-92. Basmati limited to Larkana, Jacobabad. Salt tolerant: NIAB-6, KS-282. Coarse varieties for processing.

question: aromatic rice varieties Pakistan
answer: Aromatic: Super Basmati (premium), Basmati-515, Basmati-198, Basmati-385, Basmati-2000, PK-1121, Chenab Basmati, Kissan Basmati. Export to Middle East, Europe, USA. 10-15% premium price.

question: fertilizer for basmati rice
answer: Basmati: N 100-110, P 50-55, K 50-60 kg/hectare. Per acre: Urea 3-3.5 bags, DAP 1-1.5 bags, MOP 1 bag. Zinc 10-15 kg. N in 3 splits: basal (1/3), tillering (1/3), panicle initiation (1/3).

question: zinc deficiency in rice
answer: Zinc deficiency: Brown spots on leaves, stunted growth, delayed maturity. Apply ZnSO4 15 kg/hectare at transplanting. Foliar spray 0.5% at 15-20 days. Common in flooded rice. Correct within 2-3 days after application.

question: urea application in rice
answer: Apply urea in 3 splits: Basal (1 bag/acre), 20-25 days after transplanting (1 bag), 45-50 days at panicle initiation (1 bag). Deep placement (5-8 cm) increases efficiency 30-40%. Use urea briquettes for slow release.

question: water requirement for rice
answer: Rice needs 1200-2000mm water per season. Maintain 2-5cm standing water. Continuous flooding: 1500-1800mm. AWD saves 30% water. Critical: tillering, panicle initiation, flowering. Drain 10-15 days before harvest.

question: alternate wetting and drying in rice
answer: AWD: Irrigate when water level drops to 15cm below soil surface. Saves 25-35% water. Reduces methane emissions. No yield loss if well-managed. Not suitable for heavy clay/saline soils. Pipe/pump method to measure water depth.

question: rice stem borer control
answer: Stem borer: Deadhearts, whiteheads. Control: Cartap hydrochloride 300ml/acre, Fipronil 400ml/acre, Chlorpyrifos 800ml/acre. Trichogramma cards (50,000/acre) at 30, 45, 60 days. Pheromone traps 5/acre.

question: brown plant hopper in rice
answer: BPH: Hopper burn, honeydew. Control: Pymetrozine 200g/acre, Imidacloprid 250ml/acre, Acephate 400g/acre. Avoid excessive N. Drain field for 3-4 days. Resistant varieties: IRRI-6 has tolerance.

question: rice leaf folder control
answer: Leaf folder: Leaves folded, white streaks. Control: Chlorpyrifos 800ml/acre, Quinalphos 400ml/acre, Coragen 60ml/acre. Light traps. Natural enemies: spiders, wasps. Early planting escapes damage.

question: rice blast disease control
answer: Blast: Diamond-shaped lesions. Control: Tricyclazole 400g/acre, Isoprothiolane 400ml/acre, Tilt 250ml/acre. Seed treatment with Benlate. Avoid high N. Resistant: Super Basmati (moderate), KS-282 (tolerant).

question: bacterial leaf blight in rice
answer: BLB: Yellow lesions with wavy margin. Control: Streptocycline 15g + Copper oxychloride 400g/acre. Avoid standing water at tillering. Drain fields. Resistant varieties: IR-6 has tolerance. No seed transmission.

question: rice kernel smut control
answer: Kernel smut: Black powder in grains. Control: Propiconazole 250ml/acre at heading. Seed treatment with Vitavax. Avoid excessive N. More common in Basmati varieties. Affects grain quality, not yield.

question: rice harvesting time
answer: Basmati: October-November (130-150 days). Irri: October-December (100-120 days). Harvest at 80-85% golden grains, 20-25% moisture. Late harvest: shattering, discoloration. Use reaper for cutting, thresher for separation.

question: rice yield per acre
answer: Basmati: 25-35 maunds average, 40+ with best practices. Irri: 50-70 maunds average, 80+ with hybrid. Pakistan average: 40 maunds. World average: 50 maunds. Egypt: 70 maunds. Yield gap 30-40%.

question: rice milling recovery
answer: Paddy to rice: 65-70% recovery. Head rice: 50-60%. Broken: 5-15%. Basmati: 60-62% recovery. Irri: 68-70%. Parboiled: 70-72%. Proper drying, storage improves recovery. Modern mills give 3-5% higher recovery.

question: how to parboil rice
answer: Parboiling: Soak paddy in warm water 8-12 hours, steam for 10-20 minutes, dry to 14% moisture. Increases milling recovery, nutrient retention, changes texture. Irri-6 commonly parboiled. Basmati not parboiled.

question: cotton sowing time in Punjab
answer: Sow Bt cotton April 15-May 15. Early (April) in southern Punjab, mid-May in central Punjab. After May 20: 25% yield reduction. Optimum temp 25-35°C. Late sowing increases CLCuV risk.

question: cotton sowing time in Sindh
answer: Sindh: April 1-May 15. Lower Sindh: April 1-30, Upper Sindh: April 15-May 15. Hybrid cotton: March 20-April 30 with plastic mulch. After May 15: yield reduces. Sanghar/Nawabshah: early April best.

question: best Bt cotton varieties in Pakistan
answer: Bt-121: widely adopted, yield 25-30 maunds, moderate CLCuV tolerance. Bt-703: high ginning 38-40%, yield 25-30. Bt-886: CLCuV tolerant, yield 25-30. Bt-496: early (140 days), yield 20-25. Ali Akbar-802, Sitara-009, Neelam-121.

question: CLCuV tolerant cotton varieties
answer: Tolerant: CIM-602, FH-142, Bt-886, Sitara-008, IUB-2013, Cyto-178. No variety is immune. Tolerance = less severe symptoms, yield penalty 15-30%. Avoid highly susceptible varieties. Whitefly management essential.

question: non-bt cotton varieties
answer: Non-Bt (conventional): NIAB-878 (high yield, disease tolerant), CIM-602 (CLCuV tolerant), FH-142 (heat tolerant), Cyto-178 (good staple). Yield 15-25 maunds. Bollworm control needed. Now <10% area.

question: land preparation for cotton
answer: Deep ploughing (30-40cm) every 3 years. 2-3 cultivations + planking. Bed planting: 60-70cm beds, 2 rows/bed. Ridge planting for waterlogged areas. Fine seedbed for good germination. Remove previous crop residues.

question: fertilizer for cotton per acre
answer: NPK 80-40-40 kg/hectare (32-16-16 kg/acre). Urea 2-3 bags, DAP 1 bag, SOP/MOP 0.5 bag. Boron 2-3 kg in sandy/alkaline soils. Zinc 5-8 kg. N in 3 splits: sowing, flowering, boll formation.

question: boron for cotton
answer: Boron critical for cotton. Deficiency: squares and bolls drop, poor pollination. Apply 2-3 kg borax/acre at sowing. Foliar spray 0.2% at flowering and boll formation. Increases retention 15-20%, yield 3-5 maunds.

question: irrigation schedule for cotton
answer: 8-10 irrigations. Critical: flowering (60-70 days), boll formation (90-110 days). Interval: 10-12 days summer, 12-15 days autumn. Drip: 40% water saving. First irrigation: 25-30 days after sowing. Stop at boll opening.

question: drip irrigation for cotton
answer: Drip irrigation: 60-80% subsidy under PMKSY. Initial cost Rs. 120,000-150,000/acre. Water saving 30-40%, yield increase 20-30%, fertilizer saving 25%. Fertigation: water soluble NPK. Suitable for sandy/light soils.

question: whitefly control in cotton
answer: Whitefly: Vector of CLCuV. Control: Imidacloprid 250ml/acre, Diafenthiuron 300ml/acre, Pyriproxyfen 200ml/acre, Buprofezin 300ml/acre. Yellow sticky traps 10/acre. Avoid pyrethroids. Conserve natural enemies.

question: pink bollworm control
answer: PBW: Bt cotton resistance emerging. Control: Pheromone traps 5/acre, mating disruption, Emamectin 200ml/acre, Spinosad 80ml/acre, Coragen 60ml/acre. Destroy crop residues after harvest. Rogue PBW infested plants.

question: mealybug control in cotton
answer: Mealybug: Profenofos 500ml/acre, Chlorpyrifos+Cypermethrin 400ml/acre. Ant control essential. Remove/burn affected parts. Natural enemies: Cryptolaemus, Chrysoperla. Quarantine infested fields.

question: cotton leaf curl virus management
answer: CLCuV: No cure, only prevention. 1. Resistant/tolerant varieties 2. Whitefly control from April 3. Rouging infected plants 4. Avoid highly susceptible varieties 5. Border crops (maize/sorghum) 6. Timely sowing (April-May) 7. Balanced nutrition.

question: cotton root rot control
answer: Root rot: Sudden wilting, black roots. Control: Soil solarization with plastic 4-6 weeks in summer. Trichoderma harzianum 2kg/acre in furrow. Deep ploughing. Crop rotation with non-hosts. Avoid waterlogging.

question: cotton picking time
answer: Pick every 15-20 days from October-January. Pick when bolls fully opened, fluffed white. 3-4 pickings per season. Pick early morning, avoid dew. Use cloth bags (no plastic). Keep trash separate. Grade according to quality.

question: cotton picking per acre labor requirement
answer: One person picks 50-80 kg/day. Need 8-12 persons per acre per picking. 3-4 pickings = 30-40 person-days/acre. Labor cost Rs. 500-800/40kg. Mechanized pickers rare in Pakistan.

question: sugarcane planting seasons
answer: Two seasons: 1. Spring (Feb-March) - 10-12 months, higher yield. 2. Autumn (Sept-Oct) - 16-18 months, lower yield but ratoon good. Punjab: Feb 15-March 15 spring, Sept 10-Oct 15 autumn. Sindh: Jan 20-Feb 28 spring, Aug 20-Sept 30 autumn.

question: sugarcane varieties in Pakistan
answer: CPF-248: high yield (800-1000 maunds), high sugar 11-12%, 11 months. CPF-247: ratoon excellent, yield 800-900. HSF-240: drought tolerant. SPF-234: salt tolerant. Thatta-10: Sindh variety. CSSG-668: high recovery.

question: fertilizer for sugarcane per acre
answer: NPK 250-115-115 kg/hectare (100-46-46 kg/acre). Urea 5-6 bags, DAP 2-3 bags, MOP 1.5-2 bags. FYM 15-20 tons/acre. N in 3 splits: planting, tillering, grand growth. Zinc 10-15 kg.

question: irrigation for sugarcane
answer: 15-20 irrigations. Critical: germination (0-30 days), tillering (45-90 days), grand growth (90-240 days), maturity (240-300 days). Interval: 7-10 days summer, 10-15 days winter. Skip last 2-3 irrigations for ripening.

question: sugarcane top borer control
answer: Top borer: Deadheart. Control: Cartap hydrochloride 400g/acre, Chlorpyrifos 800ml/acre at 45, 75 days. Trichogramma cards at 45 days. Removal of deadhearts. Set treatment with hot water (50°C for 30 min).

question: sugarcane red rot control
answer: Red rot: Red patches with white. Control: Resistant varieties (CPF-246, SPF-234), disease-free setts, set treatment with Carbendazim 2g/L, avoid ratooning infected fields, crop rotation, rogue infected clumps.

question: sugarcane harvesting time
answer: Harvest at 10-16 months when Brix >18%, sucrose >10%. Oct-March for maximum sugar recovery. Cut close to ground, remove trash, top leaves. Transport to mill within 24-48 hours. Delay reduces recovery 0.5% per week.

question: sugarcane yield per acre
answer: Average: 700-900 maunds/acre. Progressive: 1000-1200 maunds. Record: 1500+ maunds. Sugar recovery: 9-11%. Cane yield depends on variety, irrigation, fertilizer. World average: 1100 maunds.

question: maize sowing seasons
answer: Two seasons: 1. Spring (Jan-Feb) - harvest May-June, yield 50-60 maunds. 2. Autumn (July-Aug) - harvest Oct-Nov, yield 60-80 maunds. Spring better for grain, autumn for fodder/seed. KPK: March-April (single season).

question: hybrid maize varieties in Pakistan
answer: P-1543: high yield (80-100 maunds), drought tolerant. DK-919: 70-90 maunds, heat tolerant. P-30T60: 75-95 maunds, good grain quality. Syngenta-8441: 80-100 maunds. Pioneer-30Y87: 85-105 maunds. FH-1046: local hybrid 60-80.

question: open pollinated maize varieties
answer: Azam: 50-60 maunds, drought tolerant. Jalal: 45-55 maunds, white grain. Sahiwal-2002: 50-55 maunds. Agatti-2004: 50-60 maunds. Sarhad White: KPK variety. Seed cheaper than hybrids, can reuse.

question: fertilizer for maize per acre
answer: NPK 150-75-75 kg/hectare (60-30-30 kg/acre). Urea 4-5 bags, DAP 2 bags, MOP 1 bag. Zinc 10 kg. N in 3 splits: sowing, knee-high (30 days), tasseling (50 days). Top dress N at 8-10 leaf stage.

question: irrigation for maize
answer: 5-6 irrigations. Critical: knee-high (30 days), tasseling (50-55 days), silking (60-65 days), grain filling (80-85 days). Avoid stress at flowering - yield loss 50-80%. Drip irrigation: 25-30% water saving.

question: maize stem borer control
answer: Stem borer: Deadheart, shot holes. Control: Coragen 60ml/acre, Belt 40ml/acre, Furadan 5kg/acre in whorl. Trichogramma cards at 15, 30 days. Deep ploughing to expose pupae. Destroy crop residues.

question: maize storage pest control
answer: Maize weevil: Dry grain to 12-14% moisture. Store in hermetic bags (PICS bags). Fumigation with aluminum phosphide 2-3 tablets/ton. Neem leaves, camphor. Avoid mixing old and new grain. Sun dry periodically.

question: potato planting seasons
answer: Three seasons: 1. Autumn (Sept-Oct) - main crop, yield 150-200 maunds, stored in cold storage. 2. Spring (Jan-Feb) - 120-150 maunds, seed potato. 3. Summer (May-June) - 80-100 maunds, hills of Balochistan, KPK.

question: potato varieties in Pakistan
answer: Asterix: red skin, yellow flesh, processing, 160-200 maunds. Cardinal: red skin, 150-180. Sante: yellow skin, 150-170. Kuroda: white skin, 140-160. Desiree: pink skin, drought tolerant. FD-8-3: heat tolerant. Lady Rosetta: chips.

question: fertilizer for potato per acre
answer: NPK 200-100-100 kg/hectare (80-40-40 kg/acre). Urea 4-5 bags, DAP 2 bags, MOP 2 bags. FYM 15-20 tons/acre. Zinc 5-10 kg. Sulfur 15-20 kg. N half at planting, half at earthing up (25-30 days).

question: potato late blight control
answer: Late blight: Water soaked spots, white growth underside. Control: Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) 400g/acre, Curzate 400g/acre, Revus 200ml/acre. Spray every 7-10 days. Preventive sprays when cool (15-20°C) and humid.

question: potato common scab control
answer: Common scab: Rough, corky lesions. Control: Maintain soil pH 5.2-5.5, avoid alkaline soils, irrigation at tuber initiation, green manuring with rapeseed, resistant varieties, seed treatment with Streptocycline.

question: potato cold storage
answer: Temperature: 2-4°C for table potatoes, 3-4°C for seed. Humidity: 85-90%. Ventilation: 0.1-0.2 m³/min/ton. CIPC sprout inhibitor. Curing: 10-15°C, 95% humidity for 10-15 days before storage. Capacity: 6-8 months.

question: tomato growing seasons
answer: Rabi: Oct-Nov transplant, Jan-Apr harvest, yield 200-250 maunds. Spring: Feb-March transplant, May-June harvest, yield 150-200 maunds. Kharif: June-July transplant, Sept-Oct harvest, yield 120-150 maunds. Off-season: August-Sept in tunnels.

question: high tunnel tomato cultivation
answer: High tunnel: 18-24 ft wide, 7-8 ft height. Transplant Sept-Oct, harvest Dec-March. Price premium 2-3x. Yield 250-350 maunds/acre. Drip irrigation, plastic mulch. Rs. 800,000-1,200,000/acre setup cost, 60% subsidy.

question: hybrid tomato varieties
answer: Salar: heat tolerant, 250-300 maunds. Riogrande: processing, 200-250. Sahel: determinate, 200-250. T-1359: indeterminate, 300-350. Nageeb: long shelf life. Roma: pear-shaped, processing. Naqeeb: hybrid from AARI.

question: fertilizer for tomato per acre
answer: NPK 150-100-100 kg/hectare (60-40-40 kg/acre). Urea 3-4 bags, DAP 2 bags, MOP 1.5 bags. FYM 10-15 tons/acre. Calcium nitrate for blossom end rot. N in 3 splits: transplant, flowering, fruit set.

question: tomato fruit borer control
answer: Fruit borer: Holes in fruits. Control: Spinosad 80ml/acre, Emamectin 200ml/acre, Coragen 60ml/acre. Pheromone traps 5/acre. Remove infested fruits. Bt kurstaki spray. Early harvesting.

question: tomato early blight control
answer: Early blight: Concentric rings on leaves. Control: Mancozeb 500g/acre, Chlorothalonil 500g/acre, Score 250ml/acre. Resistant varieties. Crop rotation. Avoid overhead irrigation. Mulching to prevent soil splash.

question: onion cultivation method
answer: Nursery: Oct-Nov (rabi), May-June (kharif). Transplant 6-8 week seedlings. Spacing: 15-20 cm × 10-12 cm. Bulb initiation at 12-14 hour daylength. Harvest when 50-60% tops fall. Yield 200-300 maunds/acre hybrids.

question: onion varieties for long storage
answer: Phulkara: pungent, dark red, 6-8 months storage. Swat-1: light red, 4-5 months. Nasarpuri: red, 3-4 months. F1 Galaxy: hybrid, 4-5 months. Storage varieties have high TSS (>12%) and thick scales.

question: fertilizer for onion per acre
answer: NPK 120-80-80 kg/hectare (48-32-32 kg/acre). Urea 3-4 bags, DAP 1.5 bags, MOP 1.5 bags. Sulfur 15-20 kg (improves pungency, storage). N in 3 splits: transplant, 30 days, bulb initiation.

question: onion storage losses prevention
answer: Cure bulbs 7-10 days in shade. Store at 25-30°C, 65-70% humidity. Well ventilated structures. Maleic hydrazide 2000ppm spray 15 days before harvest reduces sprouting. Phulkara stores best. Losses 20-40% without proper storage.

question: mango orchard establishment
answer: Plant grafted plants June-August. Pit size 3×3×3 ft. Spacing: 20-25 ft × 20-25 ft (70-100 plants/acre). Fill pit with FYM 20kg, DAP 1kg, SOP 0.5kg. Staking required. Intercropping for 5-7 years. Bearing: 5-6 years.

question: mango varieties in Pakistan
answer: Sindhri: king of mangoes, golden yellow, fiberless, June-July. Chaunsa: white chaunsa (July), black chaunsa (Aug-Sept), best taste. Anwar Ratol: small, sweet, high price. Dusehri: early (June), North Punjab. Langra: green when ripe. Fajri: large fruit, late.

question: fertilizer for mango trees
answer: Per tree: FYM 50-80kg, N 600-800g, P 200-300g, K 500-600g. Apply after fruit harvest (July-Aug) and before flowering (Dec-Jan). Split application. Micronutrients: ZnSO4 0.5%, B 0.2% foliar spray before flowering.

question: mango hopper control
answer: Mango hopper: Most destructive pest. Control: Imidacloprid 250ml/acre, Confidor 250ml/acre at panicle emergence (Jan-Feb) and fruit set (March). Two sprays. Collect and destroy fallen leaves. Prune dense canopy.

question: mango powdery mildew control
answer: Powdery mildew: White coating on panicles, fruit drop. Control: Sulfur dust 5kg/acre, Karathane 400ml/acre, Tilt 250ml/acre at bud burst and 15 days later. Avoid dense canopy. Resistant: Sindhri, Chaunsa (moderate).

question: kinnow orchard establishment
answer: Plant Feb-March or Aug-Sept. Rough lemon rootstock. Spacing: 20×20 ft (109 plants/acre). Pit size 2×2×2 ft. FYM 30-40kg + SSP 1kg + MOP 0.5kg per pit. Irrigation immediately. Bearing: 4-5 years. Sargodha district is Kinnow belt.

question: kinnow varieties
answer: Kinnow (King × Willow Leaf) - 95% area. Feutrell's Early: early ripening (Nov-Dec), less juicy. Red blood: pigmented flesh. Jaffa: export variety. Musambi: sweet lime type. Kinnow Mandarin is Pakistan's main export citrus.

question: fertilizer for kinnow trees
answer: Per tree/year: N 600-800g, P 200-300g, K 300-500g. Age-based: 1 year: 100g N, increase 100g/year up to 800g. Apply 50% after fruit harvest (Feb), 50% in Aug-Sept. Zn deficiency common: spray ZnSO4 0.3% 3-4 times/year.

question: citrus canker control
answer: Citrus canker: Raised lesions on fruit, leaves. Control: Copper oxychloride 500g/acre + Streptocycline 15g. Prune affected parts, spray at new flush (March, Aug). Wind breaks. Disease-free nursery plants.

question: gram cultivation in rainfed areas
answer: Sow Oct 15-Nov 15. Seed rate: 20-25 kg/acre rainfed, 15-20 kg irrigated. Varieties: Bittle-98, Dasht, Thal-2006, Punjab-2008. One irrigation at flowering if available. Yield: 10-15 maunds rainfed, 15-20 irrigated. Thal region is main area.

question: gram varieties for Punjab
answer: Bittle-98: bold seed, yield 12-15 maunds, blight tolerant. Thal-2006: medium seed, 12-16 maunds. Punjab-2008: 15-18 maunds, resistant to blight. Noor-2013: drought tolerant, 10-14 maunds. Bhakkar-2011: 14-17 maunds.

question: gram blight control
answer: Ascochyta blight: Grayish spots, stem breakage. Control: Resistant varieties (Bittle-98, Punjab-2008), seed treatment with Vitavax, foliar spray with Mancozeb 500g/acre at disease appearance. Avoid continuous cropping.

question: mustard cultivation
answer: Sow Oct-Nov. Seed rate: 1.5-2 kg/acre. Row spacing: 45 cm. Low water requirement: 2-3 irrigations. Harvest at 110-130 days when pods turn yellow. Yield: 10-15 maunds/acre. Oil content: 38-42%. Varieties: Raya Anmol, Punjab Sarson, Khanpur Raya.

question: canola vs mustard
answer: Canola: low erucic acid (<2%), low glucosinolates, edible oil. Mustard: high erucic acid (40-50%), pungent, cooking oil. Canola varieties: Cyclone, Hyola-401, Rainbow. Yield similar 10-15 maunds. Canola gets premium price.

question: how to reclaim saline soil
answer: 1. Soil test for EC, SAR, pH 2. Apply gypsum (CaSO4) requirement based on SAR 3. Leaching with good quality water 4. Install drainage 5. Green manuring with Sesbania 6. Grow salt tolerant crops: Barley, Sugarbeet, Date palm, Eucalyptus 7. Scrape white crust. Process takes 2-3 years.

question: how to reclaim sodic (alkali) soil
answer: Sodic soil (pH >8.5, ESP >15): 1. Gypsum 2-5 tons/acre 2. Pyrites 3. Organic matter 20-25 tons/acre 4. Deep ploughing 5. Rice-wheat rotation with gypsum 6. Green manuring with dhaincha 7. Sulfuric acid amendments (costly).

question: crops for sandy soil
answer: Suitable for sandy soil: Groundnut, Guar (cluster bean), Mungbean, Millet, Watermelon, Potato (with irrigation), Date palm, Ber (jujube). Use drip irrigation, frequent light irrigation, high organic matter, mulch.

question: crops for clay soil
answer: Suitable for clay soil: Rice, Wheat, Sugarcane, Cotton, Mustard, Lentil. Requires good drainage. Avoid waterlogging. Add gypsum, sand, organic matter. Bed planting improves drainage. Deep ploughing once a year.

question: how to take soil sample
answer: 1. Divide field into uniform areas (5-10 acres) 2. Take 10-15 samples from zigzag pattern 3. Sample depth: 6-9 inches 4. Mix thoroughly, take 500g composite sample 5. Air dry, put in clean bag 6. Label with name, location, crop history 7. Send to soil testing lab. Free at Agriculture Department.

question: what is DAP fertilizer
answer: DAP (Diammonium Phosphate): 18-46-0. Contains 18% N, 46% P2O5. Water soluble, quick release. Applied at sowing for all crops. For wheat/rice: 1-1.5 bags/acre, cotton: 1 bag/acre, sugarcane: 2-3 bags/acre. Price: Rs. 7,000-8,000/bag (50kg).

question: what is SOP fertilizer
answer: SOP (Sulfate of Potash): 0-0-50 + 18% S. Potassium source for chloride-sensitive crops (potato, tobacco, fruits). Better quality, improves sugar content, fruit color, shelf life. Higher cost than MOP. Price: Rs. 6,000-7,000/bag.

question: difference between SOP and MOP
answer: SOP (K2SO4): 50% K, 18% S, chloride-free, for fruits/vegetables, improves quality, expensive (Rs. 6,000-7,000/bag). MOP (KCl): 60% K, 47% Cl, for field crops, cheaper (Rs. 4,000-5,000/bag), avoid chloride-sensitive crops.

question: drip irrigation subsidy in Pakistan
answer: Government provides 60% subsidy (80% for small farmers) for drip/sprinkler systems under PMKSY. Maximum 1 acre for vegetable, 4 acres for orchards. Apply through Agriculture Department (On-Farm Water Management). Rs. 100,000-120,000/acre after subsidy.

question: water requirement of crops
answer: Rice: 1200-2000mm, Sugarcane: 1800-2500mm, Cotton: 600-800mm, Wheat: 350-450mm, Maize: 500-600mm, Vegetables: 300-500mm. Use drip to save 30-50%. AWD for rice, bed planting for wheat.

question: how to mix pesticides safely
answer: 1. Wear PPE (gloves, mask, goggles) 2. Read label instructions 3. Use clean water 4. Triple rinse containers 5. Prepare required quantity only 6. Add adjuvants if needed 7. Do not eat/drink during mixing 8. Dispose containers properly (not in water bodies).

question: when to spray pesticides
answer: Early morning (6-9 AM) or late evening (4-7 PM). Avoid windy weather (>15 km/h), rain forecast, hot temperatures (>35°C). Temperature 20-30°C ideal. Nozzle height 50cm from target. pH of water 6-7.

question: effect of climate change on Pakistani agriculture
answer: 1. Temperature rise: wheat yield decline 6-8% per 1°C 2. More frequent heat waves 3. Erratic rains, floods, droughts 4. Glacier melt affects Indus flows 5. New pest/disease outbreaks 6. Sea intrusion in Sindh. Adaptation: heat tolerant varieties, water conservation, early warning systems.

question: how to grow wheat
answer: Wheat is a rabi crop sown from October to December. It requires loamy soil with pH 6.0-7.5 and temperature 20-25°C. Use certified varieties like Sehar-2006, Galaxy-2013, or Faisalabad-2008. Apply NPK 120:60:40 kg/ha and 4-5 irrigations. Harvest in March-May when grains are hard.

question: tell me about wheat
answer: Wheat is Pakistan's staple crop, grown on 9 million hectares. It's a rabi crop sown October-December and harvested March-May. Punjab produces 80% of Pakistan's wheat. Major varieties: Sehar-2006, Galaxy-2013, Faisalabad-2008, and Inqalab-91.

question: fertilizer for wheat
answer: For wheat, apply NPK 120:60:40 kg per hectare. Per acre: Urea 2-3 bags, DAP 1-2 bags, SOP 1 bag. Apply zinc sulphate 10-15 kg in deficient soils. Split nitrogen: 1/3 at sowing, 1/3 at first irrigation, 1/3 at second irrigation.

question: irrigation for wheat
answer: Wheat needs 4-5 irrigations. Critical stages: Crown root initiation (20-25 days), tillering (45-50 days), flowering (75-80 days), and grain filling (100-105 days). Irrigation interval: 10-15 days in winter, 7-10 days in summer.

question: pests in wheat
answer: Major wheat pests: Aphids - control with Imidacloprid; Armyworm - control with Chlorpyrifos; Termites - control with Chlorpyrifos soil treatment. Use natural predators like ladybird beetles for biological control.

question: diseases in wheat
answer: Common wheat diseases: Yellow Rust (control: Folicur 250 EC), Leaf Rust (control: Mancozeb), Karnal Bunt (control: seed treatment with Vitavax), Powdery Mildew (control: Sulfur dusting). Use resistant varieties like Aas-2011 and Punjab-2011.

question: when to harvest wheat
answer: Harvest wheat from March to May, 110-130 days after sowing. Harvest when grains are hard and moisture content is 20-25%. Dry grains to 12-14% moisture before storage. Use combine harvester for large fields.

question: when to sow wheat
answer: Sow wheat from October to December (Rabi season). Optimum sowing time is November for most regions. Delay beyond December reduces yield by 1% per day. Seed rate: 50-60 kg per acre.

question: yield of wheat
answer: Average wheat yield in Pakistan is 30-40 maunds per acre. Progressive farmers achieve 50+ maunds with improved practices. Record yields exceed 60 maunds per acre. Factors affecting yield: variety, soil fertility, irrigation, and pest management.

question: soil for wheat
answer: Wheat grows best in loamy or clay loam soil with good drainage. Ideal pH is 6.0-7.5. Soil should be rich in organic matter. Prepare field with 2-3 ploughings followed by planking. Avoid waterlogged and saline soils.

question: wheat varieties
answer: Popular wheat varieties in Pakistan: Sehar-2006 (rust resistant), Faisalabad-2008 (high yield), Galaxy-2013 (drought tolerant), Inqalab-91 (widely adapted), Aas-2011 (disease resistant), Punjab-2011 (heat tolerant), and Millat-2020 (new high-yielder).

question: cost of wheat cultivation
answer: Wheat cultivation cost per acre: Land preparation Rs. 5,000, seeds Rs. 3,000, fertilizers Rs. 10,000, irrigation Rs. 3,000, pesticides Rs. 2,000, harvesting Rs. 4,000. Total: Rs. 27,000-30,000. Subsidies available on fertilizers.

question: how to store wheat
answer: Store wheat at 12-14% moisture content. Use clean, dry gunny bags in well-ventilated stores. Treat with malathion dust @ 250g per ton. Stack bags on wooden planks, not directly on floor. Protect from rodents and insects.

question: weed control in wheat
answer: Major wheat weeds: Wild oat, Phalaris minor, Chenopodium. Control: Cultural methods (crop rotation), mechanical (hand weeding), chemical (Buctril Super 60ml/acre, Puma Super 400ml/acre). Apply herbicides 25-35 days after sowing.

question: how to grow rice
answer: Rice is a kharif crop sown May-July. It requires clay loam soil with pH 5.5-7.0 and temperature 25-30°C. Basmati varieties take 130-150 days, Irri varieties 100-120 days. Maintain standing water 2-5 cm throughout the season.

question: tell me about rice
answer: Rice is Pakistan's second staple crop and major export. Basmati rice from Punjab is world-famous for its aroma. Pakistan produces 7-8 million tons annually. Major districts: Gujranwala, Sialkot, Sheikhupura in Punjab; Badin, Thatta in Sindh.

question: fertilizer for rice
answer: For rice, apply NPK 100:50:50 kg per hectare. Per acre: Urea 3-4 bags (split application), DAP 1.5 bags, MOP 1 bag. Zinc sulphate 10-15 kg is essential for rice. Apply zinc at transplanting. Nitrogen in 3 splits: basal, tillering, panicle initiation.

question: irrigation for rice
answer: Rice requires standing water of 2-5 cm throughout the growing season. Total water requirement: 1200-2000mm. Drain the field 10-15 days before harvest. Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) can save 30% water without yield loss.

question: pests in rice
answer: Major rice pests: Stem Borer (control: Cartap hydrochloride, Trichogramma cards), Brown Plant Hopper (control: Pymetrozine), Leaf Folder (control: Chlorpyrifos). Use resistant varieties and avoid excessive nitrogen to reduce pest incidence.

question: diseases in rice
answer: Common rice diseases: Blast (control: Tricyclazole), Bacterial Blight (control: Copper oxychloride, Streptocycline), Sheath Blight (control: Validamycin), Rice Kernel Smut (control: Propiconazole). Use resistant varieties and balanced fertilization.

question: when to harvest rice
answer: Harvest rice from October to December. Basmati varieties mature in 130-150 days, Irri varieties in 100-120 days. Harvest when 80-85% grains turn golden and moisture is 20-25%. Sun dry for 2-3 days before milling.

question: when to sow rice
answer: Sow rice nursery in May-June (Kharif season). Transplant 25-30 day old seedlings. Basmati varieties: transplant in June-July. Irri varieties: transplant in May-June. Late transplanting reduces yield significantly.

question: yield of rice
answer: Basmati rice yield: 25-35 maunds per acre. Irri varieties yield: 50-70 maunds per acre. Hybrid rice can yield 60-80 maunds per acre. Pakistan's average rice yield is lower than potential due to traditional practices.

question: soil for rice
answer: Rice grows best in clay or clay loam soil that can hold standing water. Ideal pH is 5.5-7.0. Soil should have good water retention capacity. Avoid sandy soils. Zinc deficiency is common in rice soils.

question: rice varieties
answer: Basmati varieties: Super Basmati (extra long grain), Basmati-515 (high yield), Basmati-385 (good aroma), Basmati-198 (early maturing). Irri varieties: IRRI-6, KS-282, NIAB-6. New varieties: PK-1121 aromatic rice.

question: rice profit per acre
answer: Basmati cost: Rs. 40,000-45,000/acre. Yield: 30 maunds. Price: Rs. 4,500-6,000/maund. Profit: Rs. 90,000-135,000. Irri rice cost: Rs. 35,000. Yield: 55 maunds. Price: Rs. 2,500. Profit: Rs. 102,500. Export potential increases profit.

question: rice transplanting method
answer: Transplant 25-30 day old seedlings at 2-3 seedlings per hill. Spacing: 20x20cm for Basmati, 15x15cm for Irri. Plant straight, 3-4cm deep. Maintain water level 2-5cm after transplanting. Use mechanical transplanter for large areas.

question: how to grow cotton
answer: Cotton is a kharif crop sown April-June. It requires well-drained loamy or black soil with pH 6.0-8.0 and temperature 25-35°C. Bt varieties are resistant to bollworms. Harvest from October-January. Yield: 20-30 maunds per acre.

question: tell me about cotton
answer: Cotton is Pakistan's most important cash crop, earning 60% of foreign exchange from exports. Pakistan is 4th largest cotton producer. Major growing areas: Punjab (Bahawalpur, Rahim Yar Khan, Multan) and Sindh (Sanghar, Nawabshah). Bt cotton covers 90% of area.

question: fertilizer for cotton
answer: For cotton, apply NPK 80:40:40 kg per hectare. Per acre: Urea 2-3 bags, DAP 1 bag, MOP 0.5 bag. Apply boron 2-3 kg in deficient soils. Split nitrogen: 1/3 at sowing, 1/3 at flowering, 1/3 at boll formation.

question: irrigation for cotton
answer: Cotton needs 8-10 irrigations. Critical stages: flowering and boll formation. Drip irrigation saves 30-40% water and increases yield. Government provides 60-80% subsidy on drip systems. Avoid waterlogging and excessive irrigation.

question: pests in cotton
answer: Major cotton pests: Whitefly (control: Imidacloprid, Diafenthiuron, yellow sticky traps), Bollworm (Bt cotton resistant, control: Emamectin for non-Bt), Thrips (control: Acephate), Mealybug (control: Profenofos). Practice IPM with pheromone traps and natural enemies.

question: diseases in cotton
answer: Cotton Leaf Curl Virus is the most destructive disease, caused by whitefly. Control: resistant varieties (Bt-121, CIM-602), whitefly management. Bacterial Blight (control: Copper oxychloride), Root Rot (control: Soil solarization, Trichoderma).

question: when to harvest cotton
answer: Harvest cotton from October to January. Pick when bolls split open, every 15-20 days. Keep cotton moisture below 12% for storage. Pick early morning to avoid contamination. Use cloth bags, never plastic.

question: when to sow cotton
answer: Sow cotton from April to June. Optimum time: April-May for Bt varieties. Early sowing increases yield and reduces CLCuV incidence. Late sowing (after June) risks virus attack. Seed rate: 8-10 kg per acre for Bt cotton.

question: yield of cotton
answer: Bt cotton yield: 20-30 maunds per acre. Non-Bt yield: 15-25 maunds per acre. Progressive farmers achieve 35+ maunds with best practices. Pakistan's average is low (15 maunds) compared to China (35 maunds) and India (25 maunds).

question: soil for cotton
answer: Cotton grows best in well-drained loamy soil or black soil (regur). Ideal pH is 6.0-8.0. Soil should be deep, fertile, with good organic matter. Avoid waterlogged and saline soils. Prepare field with deep ploughing.

question: cotton varieties
answer: Bt cotton varieties: Bt-121 (widely grown), Bt-703 (high ginning), Bt-886 (tolerant to CLCuV), Bt-496 (early maturing). Non-Bt: NIAB-878 (high yield), CIM-602 (disease tolerant), FH-142 (heat tolerant).

question: cotton ginning percentage
answer: Ginning percentage is 33-38% for most Bt varieties. Good varieties have 37-40% ginning outturn. Higher ginning percentage means more fibre from same quantity of seed cotton.

question: how to grow sugarcane
answer: Sugarcane is planted in spring (Feb-March) or autumn (Sept-Oct). Requires deep fertile loamy soil with pH 6.5-7.5. Duration: 10-16 months. Yield: 700-900 maunds per acre. Major varieties: CPF-248, CPF-247, HSF-240.

question: tell me about sugarcane
answer: Sugarcane is Pakistan's 2nd largest cash crop after cotton. Pakistan produces 70-80 million tons annually. Major areas: Punjab (Faisalabad, Jhang, Sargodha) and Sindh (Badin, Thatta). Sugar mills provide procurement zones and timely payments.

question: fertilizer for sugarcane
answer: For sugarcane, apply NPK 250:115:115 kg per hectare. Per acre: Urea 5-6 bags, DAP 2-3 bags, MOP 1.5-2 bags. Apply 15-20 tons FYM at planting. Nitrogen in 3 splits: at planting, tillering, grand growth.

question: pests in sugarcane
answer: Major pests: Top Borer (control: Cartap hydrochloride, Trichogramma cards), Root Borer (control: Chlorpyrifos), Scale Insect (control: Dichlorvos), Termites (control: Chlorpyrifos soil treatment). Use resistant varieties and biological control.

question: diseases in sugarcane
answer: Red Rot: red patches with white spots - control: resistant varieties, disease-free setts. Smut: whip-like black structure - control: hot water treatment, resistant varieties. Rust: brown pustules - control: Mancozeb.

question: when to harvest sugarcane
answer: Harvest sugarcane at 10-16 months when juice has maximum sucrose (October-March). Cut close to ground, remove trash immediately, and transport to mill within 24-48 hours. Delay reduces sugar recovery.

question: yield of sugarcane
answer: Average sugarcane yield in Pakistan: 700-900 maunds per acre. Progressive farmers achieve 1000+ maunds per acre. Sugar recovery: 9-11%. Pakistan's yield is lower than Brazil (1200 maunds) and India (1000 maunds).

question: sugarcane planting method
answer: Plant sugarcane setts (3-budded cuttings) in furrows 90cm apart. Seed rate: 25-30 maunds/acre. Treat setts with fungicide. Plant depth: 10-15cm. Cover with soil and press firmly. Irrigate immediately after planting.

question: sugarcane ratoon management
answer: Ratoon sugarcane yields 80-90% of plant crop. After harvest, leave 5-7cm stubble. Apply Urea 2 bags + DAP 1 bag immediately. Irrigate within 3 days. Remove old roots and weeds. Ratoon lasts 2-3 cycles.

question: how to grow maize
answer: Maize is grown in spring (Jan-Feb) and autumn (July-Aug). Requires well-drained loamy soil with pH 5.8-7.5. Hybrid varieties yield 70-100 maunds per acre, open-pollinated yield 40-60 maunds. Harvest at 90-110 days.

question: fertilizer for maize
answer: For maize, apply NPK 150:75:75 kg per hectare. Per acre: Urea 4-5 bags, DAP 2 bags, MOP 1 bag. Apply zinc 10 kg. Nitrogen in 3 splits: at sowing, knee-high, and tasseling.

question: maize varieties
answer: Hybrid maize: P-1543, DK-919, P-30T60, P-33H25, Syngenta-8441. Open-pollinated: Azam, Jalal, Sahiwal-2002, Agatti-2004. Hybrids give 70-100 maunds, open-pollinated give 40-60 maunds per acre.

question: maize pests control
answer: Stem borer: use Furadan 3G at sowing. Armyworm: Karate 2.5EC. Aphids: Confidor 200SL. Maize weevil: store grains with Actellic dust. Use pheromone traps for monitoring.

question: maize profit per acre
answer: Hybrid maize cost: Rs. 35,000. Yield: 80 maunds. Price: Rs. 2,000/maund. Profit: Rs. 125,000/acre. Spring maize gives higher prices due to off-season supply.

question: how to grow potato
answer: Potato is grown in autumn (Sept-Oct) and spring (Jan-Feb). Requires sandy loam soil with pH 5.5-6.5. Use certified seed tubers. Yield: 150-200 maunds per acre. Storage: cold storage at 2-4°C.

question: fertilizer for potato
answer: For potato, apply NPK 200:100:100 kg per hectare. Per acre: Urea 4-5 bags, DAP 2 bags, MOP 2 bags. Apply 15-20 tons FYM. Zinc 5-10 kg. Split nitrogen: half at planting, half at earthing up.

question: diseases in potato
answer: Late Blight: water-soaked spots - control: Metalaxyl, Mancozeb, Ridomil Gold. Early Blight: concentric rings - control: Chlorothalonil. Black Scurf: black lesions - control: seed treatment with Carbendazim.

question: potato varieties

question: potato profit per acre

question: how to grow tomato
answer: Tomato is grown in rabi (Oct-Nov), spring (Feb-March), and kharif (June-July). Requires sandy loam soil with pH 6.0-6.8. Transplant 25-30 day old seedlings. Harvest 70-90 days after transplanting. Yield: 200-300 maunds per acre for hybrids.

question: pests in tomato
answer: Major tomato pests: Whitefly (control: Imidacloprid, yellow sticky traps), Fruit Borer (control: Spinosad, Emamectin), Aphids (control: Diafenthiuron, neem oil), Mites (control: Abamectin).

question: tomato diseases
answer: Bacterial wilt: remove infected plants. Early blight: Dithane M-45. Late blight: Ridomil Gold. Virus diseases: control whiteflies, use resistant varieties. Blossom end rot: calcium deficiency.

question: tomato varieties
answer: Roma (processing), Money Maker, Rio Grande, T-55 (hybrid), GS-600 (high yield). Cherry tomatoes gaining popularity in urban markets.

question: tomato profit per acre
answer: Tomato cost: Rs. 60,000-80,000/acre. Yield: 250 maunds. Price: Rs. 1,000-2,000/maund. Profit: Rs. 170,000-420,000/acre. Off-season production gives highest returns.

question: how to grow onion
answer: Onion is sown Oct-Dec (rabi) and May-June (kharif). Requires sandy loam soil with pH 6.0-7.0. Transplant 6-8 week old seedlings. Bulb formation at 20-25°C. Yield: 200-300 maunds per acre for hybrids. Storage: well-ventilated dry place.

question: onion varieties
answer: Red varieties: Phulkara, Swat-1, Nasarpuri. White: White Globe. Hybrids: F1 Galaxy, Red Creole. Phulkara is famous for its pungency and storage quality.

question: fertilizer for onion
answer: Onion requires NPK 120:60:60 kg/ha. FYM 15-20 tons. Apply complete dose of P and K at planting. Nitrogen in 3 splits: transplanting, 30 days, 60 days after transplanting.

question: onion profit per acre
answer: Onion cost: Rs. 50,000-60,000/acre. Yield: 250 maunds. Price: Rs. 1,500-3,000/maund. Profit: Rs. 325,000-690,000/acre. Export to Middle East increases profitability.

question: how to grow mustard
answer: Mustard is a rabi crop sown October-November. Requires loamy or sandy loam soil with pH 6.0-7.5. Low water requirement: 2-3 irrigations. Harvest at 110-130 days. Yield: 10-15 maunds per acre. Varieties: Raya Anmol, Punjab Sarson.

question: is mustard profitable
answer: Yes, mustard is profitable. Cost: Rs. 15,000-18,000 per acre. Yield: 10-15 maunds. Market price: Rs. 3,000-4,000 per maund. Net profit: Rs. 20,000-25,000 per acre. ROI: 80-150%. Good for rainfed areas.

question: mustard oil content
answer: Mustard varieties have 38-42% oil content. Improved varieties like Raya Anmol have 42% oil. Oil extraction efficiency: 30-35%. Mustard cake is valuable animal feed.

question: how to grow gram
answer: Gram (chickpea) is a rabi crop sown October-November. Suitable for sandy loam soil with pH 6.0-8.0. Requires 1-2 irrigations only. Duration: 90-120 days. Yield: 10-15 maunds rainfed, 15-20 maunds irrigated. Major area: Thal region.

question: gram varieties

question: gram profit per acre
answer: Gram cost: Rs. 12,000-15,000/acre. Yield: 12 maunds. Price: Rs. 6,000-8,000/maund. Profit: Rs. 60,000-85,000/acre. Low input cost makes it attractive for marginal farmers.

question: how to grow mango
answer: Mango is Pakistan's king of fruits. Plant certified grafts in July-August. Spacing: 10x10m. Starts bearing in 4-5 years. Full production at 10-15 years. Yield: 80-100 kg per tree. Major varieties: Sindhri, Chaunsa, Anwar Ratol.

question: mango varieties
answer: Sindhri (Sindh), Chaunsa (Punjab), Anwar Ratol (Punjab), Langra (Punjab), Dashehari (Punjab). Export varieties: Sindhri, Chaunsa to Middle East and Europe.

question: mango orchard profit
answer: Mango orchard establishment cost: Rs. 100,000/acre for 3 years. Yield: 4,000-6,000 kg/acre from year 6. Price: Rs. 40-100/kg. Profit: Rs. 160,000-600,000/acre. Export increases profitability significantly.

question: how to grow citrus
answer: Citrus (Kinnow) planting: February-March. Spacing: 6x6m. Bear in 3-4 years. Full production: 8-10 years. Yield: 1,000-1,500 fruits per tree. Major areas: Sargodha, Bhalwal, Toba Tek Singh.

question: citrus varieties

question: citrus profit per acre
answer: Citrus orchard cost: Rs. 120,000/acre for 4 years. Yield: 12,000-18,000 fruits/acre. Price: Rs. 5-15/fruit. Profit: Rs. 60,000-270,000/acre. Export to Russia, Philippines, Afghanistan.

question: how to grow tobacco
answer: Tobacco is grown in KPK (Swabi, Mardan) and Punjab. Sown in October. Harvest leaves gradually. Requires careful curing. Companies provide technical support. Virginia and Naswar types grown.

question: tobacco profit per acre

question: how to improve sandy soil
answer: To improve sandy soil: 1. Add 20-25 tons/acre FYM annually 2. Green manuring with guar or dhaincha 3. Use mulch to reduce evaporation 4. Frequent light irrigation 5. Apply zinc and iron supplements. Sandy soil is found in Thal, Cholistan, and coastal areas.

question: how to improve clay soil
answer: To improve clay soil: 1. Add sand or silt (5-10 tons/acre) 2. Apply gypsum (1-2 tons/acre) 3. Deep ploughing once a year 4. Add organic matter regularly 5. Raised bed planting. Clay soil is good for rice but requires management for other crops.

question: how to improve saline soil
answer: To improve saline (Kallar) soil: 1. Apply gypsum (2-5 tons/acre based on soil test) 2. Leach salts with good quality water 3. Grow salt-tolerant crops (Barley, Sugarbeet, Date palm) 4. Add organic matter (FYM 15-20 tons/acre) 5. Scrape white crust. Found in Sindh (Badin, Thatta) and Southern Punjab.

question: best soil for farming
